questions.q: Adipic acid, HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH, on heating gives
questions.explain: 1,6-Dicarboxylic acids lose both CO₂ and H₂O and close a five-membered carbocyclic ring, giving cyclopentanone, which has one carbon fewer than the acid. Cyclohexanone comes from pimelic acid.

questions.q: Which dicarboxylic acid forms a cyclic anhydride when heated?
questions.explain: Glutaric acid (1,5-) loses water to give a six-membered cyclic anhydride. Malonic and oxalic acids are too short and lose CO₂; pimelic acid gives cyclohexanone.

questions.q: The products of simply heating oxalic acid (without any dehydrating agent) are
questions.explain: Heat alone gives formic acid and carbon dioxide. CO + CO₂ + H₂O is the trap: that result needs concentrated H₂SO₄ to remove water.

questions.q: 3-Hydroxybutanoic acid, 4-hydroxybutanoic acid and lactic acid are heated separately. The products are, respectively,
questions.explain: A β-hydroxy acid dehydrates to the α,β-unsaturated acid, a γ-hydroxy acid closes a five-membered lactone, and an α-hydroxy acid (lactic acid) condenses in pairs to the cyclic diester lactide.
